takeaway: When websites changed their CMS in October, 1.5 left WordPress for each one that joined it, and Sanity took websites from every side.
Shops that changed their e-commerce platform in October moved to Shopify six times for each time they left it, most of them from WooCommerce.
Klaviyo runs on a third of fashion websites and is still growing 9.7% a month: in October it gained 15.5 websites for each one it lost.
Judge.me shows reviews on one in five fashion websites, and in October it gained 12.6 websites for each one it lost.
One in five fashion websites now measures its sales with the TikTok pixel, and shops added 3.3 for each one they removed in October.
Gorgias, a help desk built for shops, grew 4% a month in October, led by fashion and beauty brands.
Hospitality and food roles rose from 3.9% to 4.8% of job postings in two weeks, and to 38.8% of postings at travel and hospitality companies.
Brand marketing roles rose from 1.23% to 1.45% of job postings in two weeks, led by software and media companies.
Spotify Ad Analytics grew fastest of all, at 14.1% a month; among technologies on 1% of websites or more, Klaviyo led at 9.7%, ahead of the Reddit Pixel and Cloudflare Turnstile.
Salesforce's embedded chat lost websites fastest, 5.3% a month, ahead of Criteo, Taboola and VWO; among the most used, Universal Analytics and WordPress shrank.
Microsoft Clarity runs on 6.4% of websites against Hotjar's 4.5%, and in October the gap widened: Clarity grew 4.8% a month while Hotjar slipped.
PostHog is growing 12.1% a month on company websites, the fastest of the analytics tools in this edition, with 6.3 additions for each removal.

finding: The Front Door Moves to Cloudflare
takeaway: More than a third of websites are now served through Cloudflare, and in October 8.5 moved onto it for each one that moved off.
Next.js runs on 3.8% of websites and is growing 4.4% a month: in October 8.9 websites added it for each one that removed it.
Google has retired Universal Analytics, yet its tag still loads on 17.4% of websites, and it is coming off slowly.
Cloudflare Turnstile, a bot check most visitors never see, is growing 8.4% a month, ten times as fast as reCAPTCHA.
In the week to 24 October, 1.6% of shops that changed their announcement banner named Black Friday, four and a half times the share two weeks before.
Sales roles selling to small businesses or consumers rose from 41.5% to 44.3% of the postings that name a segment in two weeks, while enterprise roles fell below half.
Outbound prospecting still drives most sales roles, but postings that work leads coming in rose from 12.0% to 17.2% in two weeks.
